evidence: src/application/dto.ts declares PlaceOrderCommand, OrderDto and StockLevelDto plus toOrderDto/toStockLevelDto. Every use case imports its mapper from here and none builds DTOs inline.

src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts and src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts both use OrderRepository.findById, then call order.advance()/order.cancel(), then toOrderDto. State-transition rules stay in the domain.
src/application/ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts validates status with the domain's isOrderStatus instead of keeping a local copy of the status list.

src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts creates lines with OrderLine.create and reserves stock through StockReservationService.reserve. CancelOrderUseCase.ts releases stock through the same service, so the reservation logic is kept in one place.
src/application/GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts uses ProductRepository.findAll mapped with toStockLevelDto, the same pattern as the order use cases.

Minor: the not-found check `if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", ...)` appears in both AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts and CancelOrderUseCase.ts. It's two lines of boilerplate, not a duplicated business rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module is one cohesive application layer for an order/stock service. Each use-case file has a single execute method: it loads data through domain repository or service ports, calls domain behaviour and returns a DTO built by a shared mapper in dto.ts. The module's abstractions are used consistently: DomainError for all errors, toOrderDto/toStockLevelDto for all mapping, OrderRepository/ProductRepository for persistence and StockReservationService for reservation. No use case maps DTOs itself or skips the repositories. State changes are left to the domain (order.advance(), order.cancel()), and status validation reuses the domain's isOrderStatus instead of a local copy. Three minor points don't amount to a failure. AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase both repeat the same two-line not-found check, which is small boilerplate rather than a business rule. PlaceOrderUseCase checks that the customer id is present; this may repeat a rule inside the domain's Order class, but Order's source isn't provided, so it can't be confirmed. PlaceOrderCommand and OrderDto describe order lines with the same shape, which is ordinary interface data rather than a duplicated rule.
